paper.title: Ascon v1.2: Lightweight Authenticated Encryption and Hashing

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper (320-bit state, round constants, bitsliced S-box, linear layer, duplex AEAD modes and sponge hash modes); no third-party code copied. The generated known-answer strings make the source about 500 KB
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: Ascon-128, Ascon-128a and Ascon-80pq: for each, all 1089 known-answer vectors (plaintext 0..32 bytes x associated data 0..32 bytes, key 00 01 02 .., nonce 00 .. 0f) produce the published ciphertext||tag (3 x 1089 of 3 x 1089), and each published ciphertext decrypts back to the plaintext with a valid tag (3 x 1089 of 3 x 1089)

Ascon-Hash, Ascon-Hasha, Ascon-Xof (32-byte output) and Ascon-Xofa (32-byte output): for each, all 1025 messages of 0..1024 bytes (00 01 02 ..) produce the published 32-byte digest (4 x 1025 of 4 x 1025)
program sanity check, not a published value: a ciphertext with one flipped tag bit is rejected by the decryption routine for every vector

expected_values_source.what: the LWC_AEAD_KAT_* and LWC_HASH_KAT_256.txt files of the authors' ascon-c repository, directories ascon128v12, ascon128av12, ascon80pqv12, asconhashv12, asconhashav12, asconxofv12, asconxofav12, tag v1.2.7; parsed mechanically (the parser also checked that every key, nonce, plaintext, associated-data and message is the expected 00 01 02 .. pattern)
expected_values_source.url: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ascon/ascon-c/v1.2.7/crypto_aead/ascon128v12/LWC_AEAD_KAT_128_128.txt (and the six sibling files named above)
expected_values_source.note: the vectors are data, copied as numbers; the repository's code was not copied. The newer SP 800-232 Ascon-AEAD128/Ascon-Hash256 variants (different IVs) are not checked

negative_control: built with -DASCON_PB_A=11 (eleven rounds instead of twelve for initialisation, finalisation and hashing), 0 of 3 x 1089 encryptions, 0 of 3 x 1089 decryptions and 0 of 4 x 1025 digests match and the program exits 1; check.sh reports NOT REPRODUCED
not_checked: the paper's security claims, or any cryptanalysis of Ascon
the NIST SP 800-232 final standard variants (Ascon-AEAD128, Ascon-Hash256, Ascon-XOF128, Ascon-CXOF128), which use different IVs and parameters
XOF outputs longer than 32 bytes; plaintext, associated-data and message patterns other than 00 01 02 ..; keys and nonces other than the KAT's
speed or hardware-area figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the authors' published known-answer values for the inputs listed. It does not show Ascon is secure.
